subject: Insights UX + exception routing for high-cost route spikes
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, sara@acme.com
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Insights UX + exception routing for high-cost route spikes

Team —

Quick summary: Acme's analytics team surfaced repeated production bursts on a small set of inference routes that drive a disproportionate percentage of their token spend. They want an easy way in Console to:

- See per-route cost + tail-latency snapshots for a chosen time window
- Surface the top 3 callers (tenant or API key) contributing to a spike
- Attach an operator action (canary fallback / temporary throttle / add to sampling) directly from the insights card

I attached a CSV with a few real spike samples Acme shared (redacted customer ids). High-level ask: can the Insights panel have a compact, actionable view that shows cost delta, tail latency (99th/99.9th), and a 1-click route-level rollback/canary trigger?

Constraints to keep in mind: any quick operator actions must be safe (read-only for most users, gated by a role with explicit confirmation and audit logging). We should also avoid adding heavy queries that hurt Console performance.

Questions for the group:
1) Irene — engineering feasibility: can we compute the 99.9th by route for a 24h window without heavy scan? Is pre-aggregation viable?
2) Kimberly — UX: what's the smallest set of controls that lets an operator decide to apply a canary fallback or flag a route to sample?
3) Marissa — programmatic: do we want this behind a short beta and a flag for Dedicated customers first?

Attachments: spike-samples.csv (CSV, 24KB)

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Observability Product
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, sara@acme.com
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Insights UX + exception routing for high-cost route spikes

On Mon, Nov 15, 2027 at 09:14 AM Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Quick summary: Acme's analytics team surfaced repeated production bursts on a small set of inference routes...

Thanks for the context, Jonas. Technical notes / quick checks:

- Pre-aggregation: we can maintain per-route histograms (approximate quantiles) at ingest time, and roll them up hourly. That would let us return 99th/99.9th fast for sliding windows without scanning raw traces. It adds ~6-10% write cost to metrics ingestion but dramatically reduces query cost.
- Top callers: we already emit per-tenant counters. We can attach the top-3 callers per-route via a small, bounded map stored alongside the histogram—cheap to maintain if we cap the map size.
- Operator actions: the control plane already supports route-level config toggles (sampling %, fallback variant). The main work is UI & RBAC + an audit trail that captures who clicked what.

Open questions for design/ops:
- Aggregation retention: do we keep hourly histograms for 30d or 90d? 90d inflates storage.
- Canary semantics: should the console button open a 2-step modal (preview affected tenants + impact estimate) before acting? I recommend the modal.

I'll prototype an ingest-side histogram and a small test query next sprint.

Attachment: cost-breakdown-extract.xlsx (stub)

—
Irene Choi
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, sara@acme.com
Date: Thu, 18 Nov 2027 10:27:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Insights UX + exception routing for high-cost route spikes (mockups attached)

Forwarding my quick mockups — attaching a very small set of screens that try to keep the insight card compact.

Design notes:
- Primary card shows three tiles: Cost delta (%), 99th latency, 99.9th latency. Small sparkline for 24h.
- Expand -> shows top 3 callers, recent example payloads (redacted), and quick actions.
- Quick actions: "Add to sampling (5%)", "Enable canary fallback", "Open runbook".
- For canary/fallback we surface an impact estimate based on inferred QPS from top callers. If the estimate suggests >20% traffic will be affected, show an additional confirmation and optionally suggest a canary window.

Accessibility notes: keep controls keyboard-focusable and ensure the modal copies the audit text to the clipboard in case a support agent wants to paste into a ticket.

Attachment: ux-mockups-v2.png (PNG, 180KB)

Kimberly Park
Senior Product Designer, Console UX
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: sara@acme.com
Date: Mon, 21 Nov 2027 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Insights UX + exception routing for high-cost route spikes

This looks solid — thanks everyone for the rapid turn.

Action items:
1) Jonas, please create a short spec doc (1–2 pages) that lists minimum fields for the card + RBAC behavior and link it to INF-4821. Use the Google doc link (Jonas, I added a placeholder).
2) Irene, prototype the histogram ingest and a small query endpoint in the POC cluster. Keep retention to 30d for the POC. We can expand if Acme wants longer windows; we can price that as an add-on.
3) Kimberly, final mockups + keyboard flows — can you include the modal copy we discussed?
4) I'll spin up a sandbox session with Acme next Tue to walk through the mockups and collect acceptance criteria.

Also: ensure audit logs are explicit (user, route, previous sampling%, new sampling%, timestamp). That's non-negotiable for Dedicated customers.

Jonas — after you post the spec, please file INF-4821 and move to Ready for Eng. Marissa approved a small engineering allocation for the POC next sprint.

Marissa Cole
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
